key_insight: A forensic audit found that the released benchmark artifacts did not match the intended radiology VLM protocol, so several original claims had to be withdrawn.
clinical_relevance: The study is a reproducibility warning for medical-imaging AI: benchmark results can be unreliable if cohort, prompt, rendering, and analysis provenance are not tightly controlled.
method: Retrospectively audited a preserved chest-radiograph vision-language model pilot without rerunning the model or adding new annotations.
Checked prompt bindings, DICOM rendering, output completeness, label extraction, statistical comparisons, and release propagation.
Reconstructed key analysis blocks from archived artifacts to test whether reported results matched the intended protocol.
evidence_signal: Of 300 planned calls, 297 returned nonempty reports; 60 Claude calls used the same C prompt for A/B, and one reconstructed cohort changed Cochran’s Q from 154.73 to 182.29.
watch_item: Because the audit relied on archived artifacts with missing split membership and an unvalidated extractor, the findings do not establish clinical performance.
paper_title: Forensic Reproducibility Audit of a Radiology Vision-Language Model Benchmark: From Intended Protocol to Released Artifact
